instruction: Research models, papers, benchmarks and training data for a duplex assistant that uses overheard multi-party conversation to disambiguate a later user request; publish the findings as a literature-review sub-tab.
scope: Context-grounded assistance after listening to an authorized multi-party conversation; unsolicited intervention is a separate extension.
sub_questions: Which systems already listen to and participate in multi-party speech?
Which evaluations require speaker-specific context to interpret a later request?
Which resources teach or test clarification rather than guessing?
What code, checkpoints, audio, transcripts and supervision are actually released?
What changes are needed for causal, synchronized duplex evaluation and appropriate disclosure?

papers.problem: Voice assistants must bind facts, permissions and instructions to the right speaker.
papers.method: Short multi-person audio scenes end in an assistant-directed request; atomic rubrics and tool-call checks score the response.
papers.results: 1,152 cases, split evenly between English and Mandarin. English all-pass rate: Gemini 3.1 Pro 66.8%; Qwen3-Omni-30B 34.0% (Table 1).
papers.relevance: Closest benchmark to overhearing a group and acting on a later handoff.
papers.limitations: Scripted TTS, mostly turn-based evaluation; separate restraint probes are not a continuous meeting simulation.
papers.title: MSI-Bench: Evaluating Multi-Speaker Voice Interaction for Collaborative AI Agents
papers.authors: Chenxu Xiong, Dongming Shen, Yuzhi Tang, Wentao Ma, Mu Li, Alex Smola
papers.source_depth: Primary full manuscript: introduction, method, experiments and limitations/conclusion; release claims separately checked against cards/repositories.

papers.problem: An identical group-chat question can mean different things depending on who asks.
papers.method: Graph-generated enterprise conversations; queries include asker identity and six memory categories, including term ambiguity and abstention.
papers.relevance: Closest formulation of speaker-conditioned disambiguation; useful text-only control.
papers.limitations: Synthetic text; no speech timing or interactive clarification. Queries are adversarially filtered against a retrieval solver. Paper and data card differ on corpus counts.
papers.title: GroupMemBench: Benchmarking LLM Agent Memory in Multi-Party Conversations
papers.authors: Jingbo Yang, Kwei-Herng Lai, Xiaowen Wang, Shiyu Chang, Yaar Harari, Evgeniy Gabrilovich
papers.source_depth: Primary full manuscript: introduction, method, experiments and limitations/conclusion; release claims separately checked against cards/repositories.

papers.venue: arXiv preprint; author comment: NeurIPS 2026, acceptance not established
papers.problem: Duplex models need long-history speaker tracking and appropriate participation in groups.
papers.method: Moshi-derived Moshi-MTB trained in two phases: bilingual dyadic pretraining, then multi-party fine-tuning; parallel audio and word-aligned text.
papers.results: MultiTalkBench final score: Moshi-MTB 13.15, MiniCPM-o-4.5 11.05, human reference 68.74 (Table 2).
papers.relevance: Most directly relevant trained full-duplex model and released multi-party speech training data.
papers.limitations: Benchmark replaces a human participant, rather than exclusively testing a later assistant request. Persona prompts are constructed offline from transcript excerpts; audit future-context leakage.
papers.title: MultiTalk: Scaling Full-Duplex Speech Models to Long, Multi-Party, Bilingual Conversation
papers.authors: Ke Wang, Houxing Ren, Zimu Lu, Yunqiao Yang, Zhuofan Zong, Mingjie Zhan, Hongsheng Li
papers.source_depth: Primary full manuscript: introduction, method, experiments and limitations/conclusion; release claims separately checked against cards/repositories.

papers.problem: Spoken requests can remain ambiguous even after reading the preceding dialogue.
papers.method: DAMSEL audio-model customization and ASK-QA: TTS-rendered Abg-CoQA with narrated knowledge, dialogue history and simulated clarification exchanges.
papers.results: ASK-QA reports 221.8 speech hours; 5,985 / 500 / 1,345 train / validation / test conversations (§3.1).
papers.relevance: Direct source for the answer-versus-clarify behavior missing from many turn-taking tests.
papers.limitations: Narrator/user/assistant voices are not a natural multi-party meeting. Dedicated ASK-QA audio, code and trained weights were not located.
papers.title: Data-Centric Improvements for Enhancing Multi-Modal Understanding in Spoken Conversation Modeling
papers.authors: Maximillian Chen, Ruoxi Sun, Sercan Ö. Arık
papers.source_depth: Primary full manuscript: introduction, method, experiments and limitations/conclusion; release claims separately checked against cards/repositories.
papers.bibliographic_note: Author diacritics checked against PDF page 1.

papers.problem: Users need follow-up answers grounded in noisy, lengthy meeting transcripts.
papers.method: LLM-generated information-seeking dialogues over QMSum meetings, with human validation, correction and attribution spans.
papers.results: 432 retained dialogues over 225 meetings; 4,161 validated QA pairs, split 2,922 / 611 / 628 (Tables 2, 14).
papers.relevance: Closest reusable meeting-grounded assistant dialogue supervision, including follow-up questions.
papers.limitations: Text-only access to a completed meeting; no assistant-addressing or real-time clarification policy.
papers.title: Efficient Data Generation for Source-grounded Information-seeking Dialogs: A Use Case for Meeting Transcripts
papers.authors: Lotem Golany, Filippo Galgani, Maya Mamo, Nimrod Parasol, Omer Vandsburger, Nadav Bar, Ido Dagan

papers.venue: arXiv preprint; authors report acceptance to Findings of EMNLP 2026
papers.problem: A voice agent needs to know whose turn it is and resolve references across participants.
papers.method: Three simulated humans plus an agent in discussion and turn-based games; behavioral and comprehension tasks.
papers.results: Twelve evaluated agents; turn-taking, response appropriateness and complementary multi-party comprehension are evaluated.
papers.relevance: Useful speaker-attribution and reference-resolution diagnostic, distinct from Duplex-MPE.
papers.limitations: Clean synthetic speech without overlap; short scenarios and no dedicated interruption test. Public code/audio verified by 19 October 2026; the earlier repository lookup failure is historical. PDF abstract says 33% where landing-page abstract says 22%; neither is plotted.
papers.title: MP-Bench: Evaluating Voice Agents as a Multiparty Conversation Participant
papers.authors: Yi-Jen Shih, Shih-Yun Shan Kuan, Guan-Ting Lin, Kai-Wei Chang, Siddhant Arora, Shu-wen Yang, Abdelrahman Mohamed, Shinji Watanabe, Hung-yi Lee, David Harwath

papers.problem: A duplex agent should respond when addressed, not whenever someone in the room speaks.
papers.method: Continuous synthetic multi-person streams; paired explicit and implicit invitation cases test onset, silence and floor release.
papers.results: 2,000 paired scenarios / 4,000 streams; already included in the broader duplex review.
papers.relevance: Essential addressing and conversational-restraint guardrail for ambient listening.
papers.limitations: Does not by itself establish long-history intent disambiguation; dedicated evaluation audio/code release was not located.
papers.title: Duplex-MPE: Benchmarking Multi-Party Interaction in Full-Duplex Dialogue

papers.problem: A pause or mention of the assistant is not necessarily an invitation to speak.
papers.method: Text LLM plus LoRA / reasoning-trace SFT predicts SPEAK or SILENT for a target participant at utterance boundaries.
papers.results: More than 120K labeled decisions from AMI, Friends and SPGISpeech; authors report up to 23 percentage-point balanced-accuracy improvement.
papers.relevance: Released training recipe for contextual participation, separate from answer generation.
papers.limitations: Human next-speaker behavior supplies labels, not optimal assistant usefulness. Labels must not be exposed as input; split by meeting to avoid shared-history leakage.
papers.title: Speak or Stay Silent: Context-Aware Turn-Taking in Multi-Party Dialogue

papers.problem: Meeting assistants must answer inferential queries and conversational follow-ups over ASR errors.
papers.method: Manually authored meeting questions; standalone QA and follow-up conversation settings, with simulated ASR-noise variants.
papers.results: 271 manually crafted QA pairs; evaluates long-context LLMs and examines agreement between model and human judges.
papers.relevance: Useful meeting QA and noisy-transcript baseline; conversation version tests follow-up references.
papers.limitations: Transcript-only completed meetings; not a streaming speaker-addressing test.
papers.title: ELITR-Bench: A Meeting Assistant Benchmark for Long-Context Language Models
papers.authors: Thibaut Thonet, Laurent Besacier, Jos Rozen
papers.source_depth: Primary full manuscript: introduction, method, experiments and limitations/conclusion; release claims separately checked against cards/repositories.

papers.problem: Voice models lose facts that appeared earlier in speech-only history.
papers.method: MultiDialog human dialogue histories with generated, speaker-adaptive TTS recall questions and supporting utterances; native recall and RAG analyses.
papers.results: 2,612 QA pairs over 653 retained two-speaker dialogues (Table 1).
papers.relevance: Isolates spoken-context retention before adding group-level ambiguity.
papers.limitations: Dyadic, test-only recall data; full histories require the underlying MultiDialog corpus.

papers.authors: Heeseung Kim, Che Hyun Lee, Sangkwon Park, Jiheum Yeom, Nohil Park, Sangwon Yu, Sungroh Yoon

papers.method: Query-based summaries with manually selected relevant transcript spans across product, academic and committee meetings.
papers.relevance: Evidence-localization supervision and meeting-grounded pretraining; also the source of MISeD.
papers.limitations: Summaries are not clarification labels; transcripts may contain future evidence relative to a live request. Audio must be obtained from source corpora.

papers.problem: Information appropriate for one user may be private to others hearing the answer.
papers.method: Workplace group chats, target-user memories and final assistant requests; score sensitive-information leakage alongside useful content.
papers.results: 562 synthetic multi-party workplace conversations; released seeds, memories, conversations and evaluation scripts.
papers.relevance: Privacy control for deciding what overheard context can be disclosed, not merely retrieved.
papers.limitations: Text-only synthetic interactions, not consent-aware ambient speech capture.

papers.method: Multimodal sensing of speech and social cues, persona-aware LLM suggestions and proactive visual updates on AR glasses.
papers.results: Evaluation on three public datasets and a 20-participant user study.
papers.relevance: Existing ambient, proactive social-assistance system: broad proactive-help claims are not new.
papers.limitations: Visual coaching, not native speech-to-speech duplex or later-request disambiguation. Dedicated system release was not located.

papers.method: Simulated multi-party negotiation with plug-in mediators; consensus and socio-cognitive intervention evaluation.
papers.results: Social mediator improves consensus change over a generic mediator in the authors’ hard setting.

papers.problem: A wearable should isolate the wearer’s conversation rather than all nearby speech.
papers.method: Self-speech beamforming anchors a slow conversation-embedding model and a fast streaming source-extraction model.
papers.results: Real-world binaural test recordings: 11 participants, 6.8 hours (§4).
papers.relevance: Front-end resource for distinguishing a user’s conversation from an unrelated bystander group.
papers.limitations: Acoustic conversation isolation, not language-level instruction interpretation or assistant answer generation.

themes: The primary example is proactive listening plus context-grounded assistance when asked. Unsolicited intervention is a separate decision problem.
MSI-Bench and GroupMemBench already formulate speaker-scoped use of conversation history; broad claims that this task is new would be unsound.
MultiTalk supplies a close duplex backbone and synthetic group-speech recipe; MISeD supplies meeting-grounded assistant responses; ASK-QA supplies clarification behavior.
Correct answers, speaker attribution, appropriate silence and disclosure are separate outcomes. A good answer score does not establish an appropriate participation policy.
Offline transcript, participant-replacement and continuous room-audio protocols answer different questions. A public dataset card is not proof of a runnable model release.

gaps.statement: Causal context-dependent requests with interactive clarification
gaps.evidence: MSI-Bench tests a later handoff; GroupMemBench tests speaker-conditioned ambiguity; ASK-QA tests clarification. The reviewed artifacts do not establish a shared, natural-meeting, prefix-only duplex protocol combining all three.

gaps.statement: Synchronize memory updates, clarification and spoken commitments
gaps.evidence: MultiTalk and Duplex-MPE address group participation and timing, but their reported scores do not isolate whether a late correction updates the intended referent before a spoken commitment.

gaps.statement: Separate perception errors from interpretation errors
gaps.evidence: MSI-Bench explicitly compares speech and clean-transcript behavior; ContextDialog isolates speech-memory recall. Speaker-labeled transcript and oracle-diarization controls would distinguish front-end loss from reasoning failures.

gaps.statement: Retain useful context without revealing it to the wrong audience
gaps.evidence: MuPPET provides a group-disclosure test; MSI-Bench includes selective disclosure. The reviewed work does not by itself establish consent-aware ambient capture or speaker-specific retention controls.

reported_scores.title: MSI-Bench · English
reported_scores.caveat: 576 English cases; all rubrics must pass. These are different model configurations under one benchmark, not a continuous duplex success rate. Values are rounded as in the paper; its 95% Wilson intervals are omitted here.

reported_scores.title: GroupMemBench · term ambiguity
reported_scores.caveat: Text-only memory pipelines, not speech models. Same question interpretation depends on speaker-specific terminology. Backend and retrieval budgets follow the paper; these are not new experiments.

reported_scores.title: MultiTalkBench · overall
reported_scores.caveat: Composite judge/participation score, not percent correct. Human reference uses original recordings. No closed-system result is reported in this comparison. Never compare its scale with MSI-Bench accuracy.

benchmark_scope.definition: Coverage of the published evaluation protocol, not every task that could be built from the data. Model interface describes the intended input/output route; it does not imply that every capability of that model is evaluated.

rows.name: MSI-Bench
rows.speakers: Yes: 2–3 human roles plus assistant; some foreground/background speech overlaps.
rows.origin: Synthetic scripts and cloned-voice TTS; recorded ambience and sound effects are mixed in. Not natural group conversations.
rows.interface: Fixed audio cases → normalized action, answer text and optional calls. Core scoring supports audio-to-text/JSON models and speech/duplex adapters; transcript controls also exist.
rows.semantics: Yes: atomic criteria for memory, authority, disclosure, ownership, scope and constraints; judge reads normalized text/calls.
rows.tools: Yes: semantic call criteria plus separate strict name/count/argument validation. Scores proposed calls, not real service execution.
rows.timing: Limited: premature-response probes and bystander interference during an answer; live on duplex targets, approximated on turn-based targets.
rows.exclusions: No general directed-interruption repair/stop-delay, backchannel-generation, pause/transition-timing or speech-fluency/quality suite. Core answer scores alone do not demonstrate duplex skill.

rows.name: MP-Bench
rows.speakers: Yes: 3 simulated human speakers plus the agent; discussion and turn-based games.
rows.origin: Synthetic LLM-authored dialogue rendered with ElevenLabs conversational TTS; human-verified tasks. Main recordings have no overlapping speech or background noise.
rows.interface: A complete audio task is streamed to voice agents. Primarily realtime speech-in/speech-out; non-realtime voice and text-only controls are also evaluated.
rows.semantics: Yes: comprehension/speaker-name accuracy and response appropriateness from transcribed output; discussion appropriateness measures consistency, not factual accuracy.
rows.tools: No dedicated tool-call task or call validator.
rows.timing: Limited: speak/stay-silent decision after the task clip and response-onset latency for realtime voice agents.
rows.exclusions: No dedicated interruption/correction-recovery, backchannel, overlapping-input or speech-fluency/quality test. Streaming input alone does not establish these behaviors.

rows.name: GroupMemBench
rows.speakers: Yes in text: multiple named workplace-chat participants, roles, threads and timestamps; no acoustic voices.
rows.origin: Synthetic enterprise group chats generated from fictional projects and participant personas.
rows.interface: Text conversations ingested by LLM memory/RAG systems, followed by text questions and answers.
rows.semantics: Yes: speaker-conditioned ambiguity, implicit references, updates, multi-hop/temporal QA and abstention.
rows.tools: No task-level function-call correctness metric; memory retrieval is part of the evaluated pipeline.
rows.timing: No speech or duplex timing tests; ingestion/storage cost is a different measure.
rows.exclusions: No audio perception, spoken output, interruption, backchannel or live clarification exchange.

rows.name: MultiTalkBench
rows.speakers: Yes: real multi-party recordings; the model replaces a designated named participant.
rows.origin: Human recordings from meeting, dinner-party, in-car and telephone corpora; constructed alignments/persona prompts. Distinct from synthetic MultiTalkPT/FT training data.
rows.interface: Long audio conversations for full-duplex speech models; target-participant outputs are aligned and inserted into the peer transcript for offline judging.
rows.semantics: Yes: response quality, speaker/state tracking, group interaction and role-specific contributions.
rows.timing: Limited: mechanical first-to-last speech-span participation score; content/role judgments. The paper explicitly excludes direct latency/interruption-timing measurement.
rows.exclusions: Its scores do not certify barge-in stop latency, backchannel timing, acoustic fluency or tool use, despite targeting full-duplex models.

rows.name: Duplex-MPE
rows.speakers: Yes: continuous multi-party scenarios with explicit/implicit assistant addressing and other-directed speech.
rows.origin: Synthetic conversation scripts with Qwen3-TTS human-role turns, assembled into paired streams.
rows.interface: Continuous audio-only input and audible output from streaming full-duplex models with persistent state.
rows.semantics: Yes: conditional answer accuracy; semantic distinction between allowed acknowledgements and substantive intrusion.
rows.timing: Yes: fresh response onset, silence preservation and floor release after a human answers/cancels the request, including speech arriving during an answer.
rows.exclusions: No broad tool-use or speech-fluency/prosody suite; allowed backchannels are exempted from intrusion scoring, rather than scored as a standalone generation task.

rows.name: ASK-QA
rows.speakers: Three voice roles: narrator, user and assistant; a QA interaction with narrated context, rather than a group discussion.
rows.origin: Abg-CoQA text dialogues rendered with TTS, plus generated/paraphrased assistant text, injected disfluencies and noise.
rows.interface: Spoken context/history → text answer or clarification from audio-language models; turn-based simulator can extend the dialogue.
rows.semantics: Yes: answer similarity and final outcome after simulated clarification turns.
rows.timing: No simultaneous listen/speak, interruption or timed backchannel metric; interactive clarification uses successive turns.
rows.exclusions: No natural multi-party addressee competition or realtime duplex/speech-delivery evaluation.

rows.name: ELITR-Bench
rows.speakers: Multi-party meetings represented as transcripts; assistant answers a later reader's meeting questions.
rows.origin: Human meeting recordings/ASR transcripts with manually authored QA; additional transcript-noise conditions.
rows.interface: Completed-meeting text → text answers from long-context LLMs; standalone QA and follow-up conversation variants.
rows.semantics: Yes: meeting-grounded answer quality and robustness to transcript noise.
rows.timing: No audio-stream timing or duplex interaction protocol.
rows.exclusions: No acoustic speaker perception, live interruption/backchannel behavior, or spoken-output quality.

rows.name: ContextDialog
rows.speakers: Two dialogue speakers, used as user/assistant history; not a multi-person group setting.
rows.origin: Hybrid: human MultiDialog histories plus LLM-generated recall QA and speaker-adaptive TTS question/answer audio.
rows.interface: Spoken dialogue history and recall question → answer from voice interaction models; RAG and text-derived controls.
rows.semantics: Yes: recall of past user/assistant facts and use of retrieved supporting utterances.
rows.tools: No external function-call scoring; RAG is an experimental memory aid.
rows.timing: No dedicated interruption, backchannel or response-timing benchmark.
rows.exclusions: No multi-party authority/addressee policy or general duplex/speech-fluency evaluation.

rows.name: MuPPET
rows.speakers: Yes in text: workplace groups plus an assistant acting for one employee.
rows.origin: Synthetic workplace chats from manually curated seeds and generated employee profiles/memories.
rows.interface: Text group conversation and private user memories → public text answer from an LLM assistant.
rows.semantics: Yes: sensitive-information leakage and useful response content.
rows.tools: No dedicated function-call execution/argument task in this protocol.
rows.timing: No speech or duplex timing evaluation.
rows.exclusions: No audio perception, interruption, backchannel, prosody or spoken fluency; privacy norms are workplace-specific.

rows.name: Full-Duplex-Bench v1 (reference)
rows.speakers: Primarily dyadic user–model interaction; not a group ownership/authority reasoning benchmark.
rows.origin: Mixed: human CANDOR/ICC recordings plus synthetic ChatTTS interruption and pause cases.
rows.interface: Timed audio streaming with concurrent generated speech; full-duplex speech-to-speech systems.
rows.semantics: Limited: coherence/relevance/adaptability of the response following an interruption.
rows.tools: No function-call metric in v1; later Full-Duplex-Bench versions have different scopes.
rows.timing: Yes: user pauses, model backchannel frequency/timing, smooth turn transitions and user interruption responses/latency.
rows.exclusions: No speaker-scoped group task/tool correctness. Timing/behavior scores do not constitute a comprehensive speech-fluency assessment.

rows.name: Full-Duplex-Bench v1.5 (reference)
rows.speakers: User–model interaction with injected listener, other-directed and background speech; not sustained group collaboration.
rows.origin: Synthesized controlled overlap events with simulated distance/channel effects.
rows.interface: Streaming audio input during model speech; open-weight and hosted full-duplex speech systems.
rows.semantics: Yes within overlap trials: classify respond/resume/uncertain behavior after the injected event.
rows.timing: Yes: interruption versus user backchannel/other-directed/background speech, stopping and response timing, prosodic adaptation and predicted speech quality.
rows.exclusions: No general long-history speaker-scoped task/tool evaluation. User-backchannel tolerance differs from v1's model-backchannel generation task.

rows.name: Full-Duplex-Bench v3
rows.speakers: No: one user speaker per recorded input clip; the task catalogue also defines a scripted agent turn.
rows.origin: Human-recorded English speech from 12 speaker IDs, annotated for fillers, pauses, hesitations, false starts and self-corrections.
rows.interface: Streaming voice-agent evaluation over recorded user audio, with local deterministic mock APIs and generated spoken responses.
rows.semantics: Yes: task completion, semantic tool arguments and spoken response content; GPT-4o judges argument and response quality.
rows.tools: Yes: multi-step tool selection and argument correctness across four domains; pass@1 requires all expected calls and arguments.
rows.timing: Yes: turn-taking, agent-start interruption rate and first-response, tool-call and task-completion latency.
rows.exclusions: No multi-party conversation, real-service execution, dedicated user-barge-in recovery or acoustic speech-quality score. Mock APIs have zero service latency; hosted-model latency includes provider/network effects.
